audit.whatIsWrong: The packet defect is real and the header is worse than the chart: diff says FAV while diffRating says 8.5/10, tone is the red hex, and report[14] calls it a 'Hard matchup' — four fields giving three different answers on a lane Yorick wins 53.18% of over 1053 games.
audit.why: The audited mirror settled this at EVEN with rows Skill / Swain / Swain / Skill / Skill / Swain / Yorick.
audit.corrected: diff to EVEN, diffRating to 6/10, tone to the even hex, and rows 0, 4, 5 and 6 flipped in matched full/content pairs with ratings inverse to the mirror.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was given to Swain flatly, with no cooldown attached to Demonic Ascension.
audit.why: Demonic Ascension is a flat 120 seconds and its form persists only while he keeps draining champions — so denying him bodies ends it. Eulogy of the Isles is 160s at rank 1. Six is even, and Grievous Wounds is what makes it even.
audit.corrected: Six is even with Grievous Wounds up; his 120s ultimate drains everything nearby, Mist Walkers included.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nevermove was described only as 'the key skill-shot' to body-block, and Vision of Empire only as poke. Both descriptions leave out the part that decides the lane.
audit.why: Riot's Nevermove text: he launches a wave forward, it then returns to Swain and roots enemies it hits — the root is on the return trip, so the outgoing wave is safe to walk through and standing still after it passes is what gets you caught. He can then pull rooted champions closer. Vision of Empire grants Swain a Soul Fragment for every champion it hits, and Ravenous Flock turns fragments into healing and permanent maximum health — dodging the W is how you starve his scaling, not just how you avoid damage.
audit.corrected: Nevermove roots on the return, not the outgoing wave — walk through it and keep moving. Every Vision of Empire that hits you hands him a Soul Fragment and permanent health.

audit.why: Executioner's Calling early is already in report[8], and it is the right call — Ravenous Flock plus Demonic Ascension is exactly the sustain profile Grievous Wounds is for. Only the reasoning was missing, and it is now stated in the cooldowns and Do's.

notes: The header block was the worst defect here: diff FAV, diffRating 8.5/10, red tone and 'Hard matchup' all coexisted on a 53.18% lane. All four now agree at EVEN / 6/10. The Nevermove return-trip root is the single most actionable mechanic and was absent — the page's 'body-block it' advice is not wrong but it hid the free answer, which is to walk through the outgoing wave.
